target_customer: US manufacturers and fabricators with welding labor shortages, plus federal buyers and technical schools
problem: The American Welding Society projects 320,500 new welders needed by 2029 while many welders near retirement; welding knowledge does not scale.
business_model: Hardware sales of robot arms and weld cells plus paid welding intelligence software skills; open source controller
product_category: Robotic welding cells with computer vision

founders.name: Angus Muffatti
previous_startups: Unnamed prior startup reaching 1M USD revenue in 18 months (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: three published ML optimization papers, designed liquid bi-propellant rocket engines and a test facility.

founders.name: Stephen Lin
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: built systems used by mission control for 19 spacewalks.

competitors.name: Path Robotics
competitors.what: Autonomous AI welding cells (Obsidian physical AI model) and later the Rove mobile welder
competitors.funding_then: 56M USD Series B earlier; later a 300M USD Series E at 2.45B USD valuation reported November 2026

technical_complexity.rationale: Building the arm, controller, seam tracking and weld pool analysis in house is hardware plus vision plus control work for a team of three.

defensibility.rationale: Open source controller invites adoption but not lock-in; Path Robotics is far ahead on funding and customers; learning from every weld could build data over time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Path Robotics raised large rounds through 2026; no incumbent action against AMR documented.

market_need_then: AWS workforce projections of 320,500 new welders by 2029 and about 80,000 openings a year, as quoted by the company.

identity.voice_and_tone: Patriotic and mission framed (American-made, American welding)

branding.brand_signature: Product names Rosie (arm) and War Machine (weld cell)

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable product names and an American-made angle, but no press about the brand found; the company name itself is generic.

outcome_analysis: Advanced Metal Research is a Spring 2026 YC company that went from selling a welding cell concept to shipping its own robot arm and open source controller. It faces a far better funded rival in Path Robotics, so the result depends on cost, American-made positioning and the data advantage from learning on every weld. No outcome is known yet.
notes: Dealroom shows a 125K USD seed entry with no investors; single aggregator, unverified, not recorded as a round. Founder education not listed anywhere opened. Competitor entries are current-era (2026) players because no early-2025 dated coverage was found; Path Robotics's later rounds are not as of founding. YC says Los Angeles, company site says Hawthorne, California.
